observations.code_quote: if len(row) > len(headers) and not any(cell.strip() for cell in row[len(headers) :]):
observations.behavior: Adds CSV parsing normalization to handle trailing delimiters and ragged rows without treating them as malformed.
observations.posthog_connection: Connects warehouse ingestion reliability by allowing Checkout.com reports with common layout variants (trailing commas, missing end-of-row fields) to parse successfully rather than failing or silently truncating.

observations.behavior: Raises an exception when no valid data rows are parsed from a file, while distinguishing this from header-only files which return empty results.
observations.posthog_connection: Prevents silent failure where financial history is lost; distinguishes between legitimate quiet periods and genuinely corrupted report files.

observations.behavior: Adds tests asserting that exceeding the skipped-row threshold raises an error, and that all-malformed files also fail.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection against previously reported behavior where zero-parsed files were accepted, establishing expected failure modes.

review.reason: The change adds bounded CSV parsing robustness: it normalizes trailing delimiters and ragged rows without warning, while raising errors only for truly unparseable content or excessive malformed ratios. This prevents silent under-loading of warehouse tables. The tier does not reach 3 because there is no broader systemic risk reduction demonstrated across multiple connectors or critical paths, nor claims of wider benefit supported by other components.
review.posthog_relevance: Warehouse ingestion reliability; Checkout.com reports represent recoverable financial data. Preventing silent truncation protects historical records from being dropped during scheduled imports.
review.uncertainty: Assessment limited to this chunk; unknown if similar issues exist elsewhere in PostHog’s warehouse sources.
